full_judgment:
2. The relevant facts necessary for disposal of the rule, are the petitioners-plaintiffs instituted the above noted title suit for declaration of title in 'Ka' schedule land and recovery of Khas possession in the `Kha' schedule land shown in the plaint against the opposite parties-defendants with the contentions that Sheikh Jobbar Ali was owner of 1/2 share in the lands of the suit holding and Abed Ali had a share to the extent of less than 1/12 share in the land measuring .52 acres as recorded in P.S. and S.A. Plot No. 979. He was in exclusive possession in the said Plot by way of amicable partition and the P.S. Khatian No. 138 was recorded accordingly. The previous owner Sheikh Jobbar Ali died leaving two sons in Abdul Sattar, Fazu Mia and two daughters namely Mosammat Amironnessa and Samirunnessa. One son and one daughter of the previous owner namely Abdus Sattar and Amirunnessa sold .22 acres of land out of .52 acres of the suit plot to Chini Mia by a registered kobala dated 26.8.1961. The name of the said purchaser was duly recorded in the S.A. Khatian and R.S. Khatian. Therefore, Chini Mia transferred .473 acres (Ka Schedule) to the plaintiffs by a registered kobala dated 26.6.1979. The plaintiffs started possession through cultivation of vegetable in some portion and also erected a tin shed on some area. On 6.9.1991, all on a sudden, the defendant 2 dispossessed the plaintiffs by force from the `Kha' schedule land measuring `o330 acres out of the "Ka' schedule land and dismantled the dwelling structure of the plaintiffs therefrom. As such, the plaintiffs filed the present suit. 

 10. In view of the aforesaid evidence on record, the learned Assistant Judge appears to have rightly decided that the plaintiffs acquired title and possession in the suit land by the earlier purchase and that they held possession in the 'Ka' schedule land. But subsequently the defendants dispossessed them in the year 1991 long after execution and registration of the plaintiffs purchase deed. But the learned Subordinate Judge, without considering and controverting those findings of the trial court based on evidence, dismissed the suit by introducing a new ground to the effect that since both the parties were co-sharers in the suit holding, which had not been partitioned by metes and bounds, the plaintiffs cannot get decree for declaration their exclusive title and recovery of Khas possession. Neither of the parties raised the question of undivided share at the time of trial and no pleading to that effect is available. It is true that the S.A. Khatian was recorded in the name of Chini Mia, predecessor of the plaintiffs, along with many others including some of the heirs of Abed Ali and Sk. A. Jobber and the said purchase land of the plaintiffs has not yet been separated by mutating the names of the plaintiffs. But the fact remains that the specific possession of Sheikh Jobbar Ali against the suit Plot in P.S. Khatian has not been challenged by saying that the share and possession of Sheikh Jobbar Ali was wrongly inserted in the said P.S. Khatian (exhibit. Kha), Moreover, the plaintiffs are found to have been in possession since 1979 and the defendants subsequently dispossessed them in 1990-91 by taking kobala from the heirs of Abed Ali, whose title and possession in the lands sold is yet to be established. Because, he had a very small share in the entire suit holding as recorded in the P.S. Khatian. Even, if, it is conceded that Abed Ali's heirs had some interest in the suit plot, the extent of their share is required to be established first and then the new purchasers like the defendants can be allowed to take possession from other co-sharers through the process of law. In this respect, the case decisions reported in 11 D.L.R. (SC). 78 and 12 D.L.R. 708 can be relied upon. It is held in those decisions that the possession of specific portion of lands by the purchaser in joint possession is entitled to get possession thereof till the lands are partitioned. In the present case, if the defendants want to seek relief on the basis of their purchase deeds, they are legally entitled to seek partition to get their share, even if any, through the court. In no way, they can be allowed to take law in their own hands and invade possession of other co-sharers in the lands.
